title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
summary: A comprehensive 10-week course introducing high school students to AI concepts, ethics, and hands-on projects.
description:
## Overview

This semester-long course guides students through the foundations of artificial intelligence, from pattern recognition to neural networks.

## Units

1. What is AI?
2. Machine learning basics
3. Neural networks
4. AI in society
5. Capstone project

## Outcomes

Students will be able to explain how AI systems work, evaluate ethical implications, and build a simple ML project.

title: Daily AI Warm-Up Snapshots
summary: Quick 15-minute classroom starters that spark discussion about AI in everyday life.
description:
## How to use

Each warm-up includes a prompt, discussion questions, and an optional extension activity. Designed for bell-ringer use.

## Topics covered

- AI in apps students use daily
- Spotting AI-generated content
- Asking good questions about AI claims

title: Elementary AI Explorations
summary: Age-appropriate lessons introducing K-5 students to how computers learn from examples.
description:
## Lesson series

Four hands-on explorations using unplugged activities and simple digital tools.

## Big ideas

- Computers can find patterns
- AI needs good data
- People train AI systems

No prior coding experience required for teachers or students.

title: AP Computer Science AI-Aligned Units
summary: Supplemental units mapping AI literacy content to AP CS Principles learning objectives.
description:
## Alignment

These units bridge AP CSP big ideas with contemporary AI topics including data, algorithms, and societal impact.

## Includes

- Unit overviews with timing
- Lab activities
- Practice assessment items

title: High School AI Project Set
summary: Five open-ended projects where students design, build, and reflect on AI-powered solutions.
description:
## Projects

1. Bias audit of a dataset
2. Chatbot design challenge
3. AI tool evaluation report
4. Deepfake detection investigation
5. Career pathways research

Each project includes rubrics, checkpoints, and presentation guidelines.

title: Deepfakes & Media Literacy: The R.E.A.L. Approach
summary: A quick guide for educators on teaching students to Recognize, Evaluate, Authenticate, and Limit spread of synthetic media.
description:
## The R.E.A.L. framework

- **Recognize** signs of synthetic media
- **Evaluate** source and context
- **Authenticate** using verification tools
- **Limit** sharing of unverified content

Includes classroom discussion prompts and a one-period lesson outline.

title: AI Grading Practices: A Guide for Educators
summary: Practical guidance on when and how to use AI-assisted grading while maintaining fairness and transparency.
description:
## Key questions

- What tasks are appropriate for AI assistance?
- How do you disclose AI use to students?
- What safeguards prevent bias?

Includes decision trees and sample policy language for schools.

title: Evaluating AI Tools for the Classroom
summary: A rubric-based framework for assessing AI ed-tech tools before adoption.
description:
## Evaluation criteria

1. Data privacy and FERPA compliance
2. Pedagogical fit
3. Bias and accuracy
4. Transparency of AI use
5. Cost and sustainability

Use the included scorecard in department or admin review meetings.

title: LLM Basics for Classrooms
summary: An accessible explainer on how large language models work, designed for teacher PD or upper-grade students.
description:
## What you'll learn

- How LLMs are trained
- Why they sometimes "hallucinate"
- Prompt engineering fundamentals
- Classroom-appropriate use cases

Includes a live demo script and common misconceptions handout.

title: Family Conversation Starters About AI
summary: Discussion prompts helping families talk about AI tools, privacy, and digital citizenship at home.
description:
## For families

Ten conversation cards covering topics like chatbots, social media filters, homework help apps, and online safety.

No technical background needed — each card includes context and follow-up questions.

title: Student Data Privacy in the AI Era
summary: A guide covering FERPA basics, vendor agreements, and student rights when schools adopt AI tools.
description:
## Topics

- What data AI tools collect
- FERPA and COPPA overview
- Questions to ask vendors
- Student digital rights

Includes a checklist for IT and curriculum leaders.

title: AI Critical Thinking Framework
summary: A reusable framework helping students analyze AI claims, outputs, and limitations across subjects.
description:
## The framework

**Ask → Inspect → Contextualize → Decide**

Apply across ELA, social studies, science, and CS. Includes cross-curricular lesson seeds and wall-poster graphics.

title: Middle School AI Ethics Unit
summary: A three-lesson unit exploring fairness, bias, and responsibility in AI systems for grades 6-8.
description:
## Lessons

1. What is bias in AI?
2. Who is responsible when AI fails?
3. Designing for fairness

Currently under review by the curriculum team.

title: AI Careers Exploration Module
summary: Interactive activities introducing students to diverse career paths in AI beyond coding.
description:
## Activities

- Career card sort
- Day-in-the-life profiles
- Skills mapping exercise

Pending final review before publication.

title: Neural Networks Unplugged (Draft)
summary: Draft lesson using paper-based activities to demonstrate how neural networks learn from data.
description:
## Draft status

Early draft — not yet reviewed. Uses a paper "neuron" activity to model weighted inputs.

Target: middle school science classes.

title: Build a Classroom Chatbot (Draft)
summary: Draft project guide for students creating a simple rule-based chatbot with ethical use guidelines.
description:
## Draft status

Work in progress. Will include step-by-step build instructions and a reflection journal.

Needs pilot testing in two classrooms.
